body.text: First reconstruction recorded as r0004, format VALID with partial quality. MANO has 360 valid hand frames and mask IoU .858, but validation finds poor thumb opposition, 13.2mm hand/object penetration and 45.3 percent distal-finger intersection frames. Frame inspection shows occlusion permits object-center drift beneath the hand; image-only fitting has moved the white housing center rightward away from its visible patch. Next reconstruction change adds a translation prior under occlusion, followed by shared hand/object depth fitting. The clearer black interval currently estimates 75.1 degrees relative to the hand, about object axis (0.973,0.227,-0.039), with 20.7 degrees wrist motion; these remain uncertain, prior-dependent estimates.

The provided unchanged MANO fitter was run first as required. Its contact term rewards only the closest hand probe, so high contact fraction can coexist with a distant thumb, and it has no finger self-collision term. I am refining with an agent-owned copy under research/mano_contact: add explicit thumb plus an opposing-finger contact loss and a distal-finger capsule-separation penalty, retaining silhouette, HaWoR, MANO prior and temporal terms. Original installed code remains unchanged. The new losses are physical inference, not additional video measurements; configurations and before/after checks will be recorded.

Contact-aware reconstruction refinement improves thumb contact to 99.2 percent white and 100 percent black; opposed grasp fractions are 96.9 and 92.4 percent. Both objects now pass the supplementary fingertip and anatomy checks. Visible-scene IoU is .710 white/.693 black, hand mask IoU .861. Residual penetrations remain 12.77mm white/9.29mm black and finger intersections 34.8 percent, so the reference remains physically partial. Next refinement uses all hand vertices for penetration and stronger distal-finger separation. A [redacted] geometric focal check gives a broad minimum around 1.0–1.2k px (7.8px noisy landmark RMS), consistent with retaining the 1084px prior; it does not establish precise calibration. Both reconstructed resting arrangements drift less than 0.4mm in a one-second MuJoCo rest test.

Dense release review corrects white contact through frame213 (7.10s) and black through387 (12.90s); the prior black phase wrongly included post-release frames. Shared table support is now enforced after white165 and black355, instead of letting contact fitting raise already placed objects toward the hand. The hand is refitted against this corrected scene. Anatomical palm-normal sign is derived from the right-hand MCP fan, not chosen from uncertain object depth; white palm is about 11 degrees from down, black about 69 degrees, showing distinct but both plausible demonstration wrist poses. I am also repairing black segmentation dropouts rather than labeling every absent SAM3 mask as true occlusion.

The 12-hour run did not produce a reliable turning skill. Final verification r0188, based on fresh final gate r0181, failed my criteria: 26/192 successes (13.5%, 95% Wilson 9.4–19.1%), zero hardware violations; white 12/99, black 14/93. Only settling is mastered. The unmastered turning prototype and exact evaluated policy remain available with simulation, meshes, starting poses, interface, source/weight catalog, curves and videos. There are no target rounds or submissions.

What worked: reconstruction3 passed the required validator; the full anatomical wrist frames corrected an early retargeting error. Physical reference optimization proved both primitives, with turning 41/64 in its feasibility suite. Shared CPU/GPU models and the provided controllers achieved noisy outcome parity for the chosen full policy. The PPO settling skill passed 64/64. All 26 final successes reproduced, and the inference-only runtime reproduced the illustrated successes without the privileged critic. Their geometry audit found object–hand indentation below 0.684 mm.

What failed: the selected turning policy stayed at the narrow 78-reference curriculum stage and never mastered the turn. Support loss during transfer, wrong orientation despite retained support, and later drift dominated. Reward, curriculum, observation, action-space and PPO credit-assignment variants did not earn replacement of the13/64 development incumbent. Larger batches improved throughput 3.67 fold, but that improvement came late. The corrected extra12s holding test retained tolerances for only 11/26 successful end states. Reconstruction uncertainty, axis/duration deviations and the prepared grasp family limit imitation and transfer claims. The records retain the late montage review, corrected object/timing label, and prepublication duration bug rather than hiding them.

What I would try next: first improve a robust physical/PPO teacher across the intended grasp and parameter ranges, then widen training from truly master…
